answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works like a fee at the summit gate: every identity must post a bond that is slashed when peers catch it vouching for a clone of itself. A thousand fake agents therefore cost a thousand bonds, all forfeit at once, so the tide of clones becomes a net loss rather than cheap influence. Trust also passes through a prism of independent attestations that split each newcomer across unrelated verifiers, and colluding clusters stay behind their own shared bonds, which peers discount.
